subject: Igbo
examFormat: The syllabus aims to prepare candidates for the Board's UTME in Igbo and to enable them to: communicate and read effectively in Igbo; analyse issues in the language; interpret and explain figurative and idiomatic expressions in Igbo; and apply Igbo literature to their daily life experiences and demonstrate Igbo cultural values. It has four sections: A Languages (Asụsụ), B Literature (Agụmagụ), C Customs and Institutions (Omenala na Ewumewu), D General and Current Affairs. Comprehension is one passage of about 150 words.
excluded: Two Igbo glosses in the Current Issues list (the HIV/AIDS, cancer and coronavirus line) were truncated in the extraction, so only their English names are kept. The prescribed set texts (Jụọ Obinna, Akọnuche with its 20 selected poems, Otu Mkpịsị Aka) are listed without a stated year range because the syllabus gives none.

topics.name: Essay (Edemede)
objectives: identify the basic principles of essay writing
use words and expressions appropriate to a particular topic
differentiate between different essay types
describe the characteristics of essay types
compare different types of essay
criticize other people's essays
topics.content: Basic principles of essay writing: introduction, body and conclusion. Basic essay types and their characteristics: narrative (Akọmakọ), descriptive and expository (Nkọwa na Nkọwami), argumentative (Mgbagha/Arụmarụụka), speech making (Ekwumekwu), letter writing (Edemleta), dialogue (Mkparịtaụka).

topics.name: Comprehension (Aghọtaazaa)
objectives: explain the meanings of difficult words
give correct answers
differentiate between figurative and idiomatic expressions from the passage
deduce conclusion(s) based on the passage
topics.content: One passage of about one hundred and fifty (150) words.

topics.name: Sounds and Sound Patterns (Ụdaasụsụ na Usoro Ụdaasụsụ)
objectives: identify vowels, consonants and syllabic nasals
distinguish between the speech sounds of the Igbo language
recognise semi-vowels ('m' and 'n') and nasal homogeneity
divide words into syllables
identify the vowel groups in Igbo
describe vowel assimilation, vowel elision and consonant elision
assign tone marks appropriately
topics.content: Vowels and consonants (Ụdaume na mgbochiume). Sound patterns/processes: syllabic nasals (ụdaimi); semi-vowel (Myiriụdaume); nasal homogeneity (ndagba myiriụdaume); syllable structure (nkeji mkpụrụokwu); vowel harmony (ndakọrịta ụdaume); vowel assimilation (olilo ụdaume); vowel elision and consonant elision (ndapụ ụdaume na ndapụ mgbochiume). Tone and tone marking (Ụdaolu na Akara ụdaolu).

topics.name: Spelling and spelling rules (Nsupe na Iwu Nsupe)
objectives: detect words written correctly in Igbo
determine appropriate word division in Igbo

topics.name: Igbo Orthography (Mkpụrụedemede Igbo)
objectives: indicate the Igbo orthography
distinguish between the Igbo and English orthography

topics.name: Dialect and Standard Igbo (Olundị/Olumba na Igbo Izugbe)
objectives: differentiate between standard Igbo and dialects
use standard Igbo in their writings

topics.name: Igbo Word Derivation (Usoro Mmụbaokwu n'Igbo)
objectives: differentiate between loan and coined words
identify loan words and loan-blends in Igbo
spell Igbo words appropriately
topics.content: Processes of word derivation: coinages, loans and loan-blends (Mmụbawanye mkpụrụokwu site n'usoro mmepụta, mkpụpụta, mbite na mbiọgwa).

topics.name: Grammar (Ụtọasụsụ)
objectives: differentiate between grammatical categories
identify parts of speech and their functions
differentiate between types of affixes and their functions
determine types and characteristics of morphemes
identify words, phrases, clauses, sentences, their types and characteristics
topics.content: Parts of speech (Nkejiasụsụ): nominals (Mkpọaha), verbs (ngwaa), adjectives (nkọwa), adverbs (nkwuwa), affixes (mgbakwunye), enclitics (nsokwunye), etc. The structure, types and characteristics of the morpheme (Ndokọ, ụdị na njirimara mọfịm): free and bound (nnọọrọonwe na ndabe). The word (mkpụrụokwu); the phrase (nkebiokwu); the clause (nkebiahịrị): nominal, adverbial and adjectival clause (kemkpọaha, kenkwuwa na kenkọwa); the sentence (ahịrịokwu): simple (mfe), compound (ukwu), complex (mgbagwọ), etc.

topics.name: Translation (Ntụgharị)
objectives: translate English into Igbo and vice versa
communicate effectively in Igbo and English

topics.name: Literary devices (Atụmatụokwu)
objectives: identify all literary devices in the passages
interpret literary devices
differentiate between types of literary devices
use Igbo literary devices appropriately
topics.content: Literary devices such as alliteration (bịambia mgbochiume), assonance (bịambịa ụdaume), parallelism (kwunkwugha), metaphor (mbụrụ), simile (myiri), hyperbole (egbeokwu), personification (mmemmadụ), proverbs (ilu), etc.

topics.name: Oral Literature (Agụmagụ Ọnụ/Agụmagụ Ọdịnala)
objectives: create folk stories, chants, riddles, oral drama etc
analyse various genres of oral literature
present ideas/formulae in accordance with underlying principles
apply the lessons of oral literature to their everyday life
topics.content: Folktales (ifo), myths (nkọmịrịkọ), legends (nkọkịrịkọ), poems (abụ), songs (uri), chants (mbem), riddles (agwụgwa), oral drama (ejije ọnụ), tongue-twister (okwuntụhị), etc.

topics.name: Written Literature: Prose (Iduuazị)
objectives: interpret the text
isolate the characters in the book
identify figurative and idiomatic expressions in the text
analyse the text
identify the author, publisher and date of publication
draw moral lessons from the text

topics.name: Written Literature: Poetry (Abụ)
objectives: compare the types and themes of the poems
relate the poet's idea to the contents of the poems
compare figurative and idiomatic expressions in the poems
analyse the structures of the poems
apply acquired knowledge and moral lessons from the poems to their daily lives
topics.content: Prescribed poetry text: Akọnuche by Inno Ụzọma Nwadike (2014), Obosi: Pacific Publishers Ltd. Abụ ndị a họpụtara (selected poems, with pages): 1. Ọchịchị 18-19; 2. Onye Ndu 22-23; 3. Nne Ọma 29-30; 4. Oke Ọchịchọ 40-41; 5. Asịla M Na Ọ Dị Mma 53-54; 6. Ihe Ụwa 60-61; 7. Jiri Nwayọ 62-63; 8. Eziokwu 65-66; 9. Mma 67-69; 10. Nwanyị 92-94; 11. Aja Ala 101-103; 12. Ala Igbo 108-111; 13. Ndụ M N'ụwa A 131-132; 14. Ọjị 150-151; 15. Ụwa Emebighi 151-154; 16. Amamihe 168-169; 17. Ndụ Nwaanyị 178-180; 18. Nna M Ọgọenyi 181-184; 19. Ụlọakwụkwọ 192-193; 20. Akwa Nnabuenyi Ugonna Bere 249-252.

topics.name: Written Literature: Drama (Ejije)
objectives: identify the type of drama the text belongs to
determine the themes in the text
identify the story lines
find out the characters in the book
appreciate the language style of the play
appraise the social problems raised by the author in the play
apply acquired knowledge to their personal lives
identify the moral lessons from the drama text

topics.name: Customs and Institutions (Omenala na Ewumewu)
objectives: describe the customs of their people
determine the rules and regulations guiding specified aspects of the culture and tradition of the Igbo people
describe the importance of the aspects of Igbo culture
identify changes that have occurred as a result of civilization
explore their environment for a better appreciation of their culture
topics.content: Igbo customs and institutions as categorized in the eighteen subtopics.

subtopics.name: Ekele dị iche iche
objectives: describe the customs and institutions on: ekele ụtụtụ, ehihie, anyasị, nri, onye nọ n'ọrịa, nlakpu, ọrụ, etc

subtopics.name: Alụmdi na nwunye
objectives: describe the customs and institutions on: alụmdi na nwunye, ịgba alụkwaghịm

subtopics.name: Ọmụmụ na ile ọmụgwọ
objectives: describe the customs and institutions on: ọmụmụ na ile ọmụgwọ, ikupụta nwa, ibi ugwu, ịgụ aha, ịzụ ahịa nwa, ịhụ eze

subtopics.name: Echichi
objectives: describe the customs and institutions on: Nze na Ọzọ, Eze/Obi/Igwe, Iyọm/Lọọlọ

subtopics.name: Ike ekpe, iri ekpe, ịkwa ozu
objectives: describe the customs and institutions on: ike ekpe, iri ekpe, ịkwa ozu, ịgba mkpe

subtopics.name: Ụmụnna, ụmụọkpụ/ụmụada, iyomdi, nwadiala
objectives: describe the customs and institutions on: ụmụnna, ụmụọkpụ/ụmụada, iyomdi, nwadiala

subtopics.name: Ọgbọ/ebiri/uke, ọhanaeze, ezinaụlọ
objectives: describe the customs and institutions on: ọgbọ/ebiri/uke, ọhanaeze, ezinaụlọ

subtopics.name: Arụ na nsọala
objectives: describe the customs and institutions on: ihe nsọ, anụ nsọ, osisi nsọ, ebe nsọ

subtopics.name: Ọchịchị Ọdịnala
objectives: describe the customs and institutions on: Igwe/Eze, Nze na Ọzọ, ụmụnna, ezinaụlọ, ụmụọkpụ/ụmụada, otu ọgbọ

subtopics.name: Nnabata ọbịa, ọji na ịtu nzu
objectives: describe the customs and institutions on: nnabata ọbịa, ọji na ịtu nzu, itu aha, ịkwọ aka ụtụtụ, ịgọ ọfọ

subtopics.name: Ihe ofufe
objectives: describe the customs and institutions on: ịgba afa, ịchụ aja, ịgọ mmụọ, ofufe

subtopics.name: Ngwa ofufe
objectives: describe the customs and institutions on: ọfọ, ikenga, okpesi

subtopics.name: Nkwenye
objectives: describe the customs and institutions on: ịdụ isi/ịṅụ iyi, ịgba ndụ, orikọ, ịlọ ụwa, ọgbanje, nrọ, ihi anụ, ịha/ịchụ mmiri, etc

subtopics.name: Akụnaụba
objectives: describe the customs and institutions on: inwe ala, ike ala, iri ekpe, elulu (ịkpa ọkụkọ, ewu, etc)

subtopics.name: Abamaba
objectives: describe the customs and institutions on: mmọnwụ, ọkọnkọ, ekpe, ọmabe, odo, dibịa, etc

subtopics.name: Egwuregwu
objectives: describe the customs and institutions on: mgba, egwu ọnwa, ikpọ ọga, ịzụ nchọ, ịzụ okwe, ịgba/ịchọ oro, etc

subtopics.name: Akaọrụ ndị Igbo
objectives: describe the customs and institutions on: ọrụ ugbo, ịkụ azụ, ịkpụ ụzụ, ịzụ ahịa, ịtụ ihe ọtụtụ, ịchụ nta, ime dibịa, ịkpụ ite, etc

subtopics.name: Emume
objectives: describe the customs and institutions on: Ọfala, ịbọ ụzọ, ịwa ji/iri ji, igbu ewu ukwu, iru mgbede, ịwa akwa, akwamozu, ịgụ afọ, etc

topics.name: Topical issues in Igbo language, literature and culture
objectives: identify some dates, themes and functions of Ahịajiọkụ, Odenigbo and Ọhaneze Ndi Igbo Lectures
identify authors, publishers and dates of publication of various textbooks in Igbo
acquaint themselves with the functions and contributions of the Igbo Studies Association (ISA)
topics.content: Section D: General and Current Affairs (Ihe Ndị na-eme Ugbua). Topical issues in the Igbo language, literature and culture, e.g. Ahịajiọkụ, Odenigbo lectures and Ọhaneze Ndị Igbo; authors, publishers, dates and places of publication of works in Igbo; Igbo Studies Association (ISA).

topics.name: Current Issues (Okwuakpụnọnụ)
objectives: acquaint themselves with current issues
examine their effects
suggest remedies to the problems
topics.content: Item writers should also choose their topics for comprehension exercises from current issues such as: HIV/AIDS, cancer and coronavirus; drug abuse (Ịṅu Ọgwụ Agharaaghara); cultism (Otu Nzuzo); rights of women and children (Oruuru Ụmụnwaanyị na Ụmụaka); human rights violation and child abuse (Ịnapụ Mmadụ Ikike na Mmetọ Nwata); religious conflicts (Nsogbu Ndọkụrịta Ekpemekpe Ụka); kidnapping (Ntọrọ Mmadụ).
